VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` also marks tools available on timeout, not just on missing binary. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, while each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise returns `[]`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. Consequence: a hung tool is reported healthy/available and contributes zero diagnostics, indistinguishable from a clean scan.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually run analysis or tests in a source-faithful sandbox for any fix that depends on imports or neighboring project files. It copies only the single target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = tmpdir / basename(target_path)`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file; if `test_cmd` is provided, it runs the original command in `cwd=tmpdir` without rewriting paths. Evidence: the sandbox contains just one file, no package tree, no sibling modules, no project config, and no tests unless the caller’s command happens to be tmpdir-relative. This violates the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” behavior for normal module-level fixes in a multi-file package.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix verdicts can be silently wrong in both directions. A harmful fix can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL because cross-file breakage is invisible when imports cannot resolve or dependent modules are absent. A valid fix can be marked UNEVALUABLE/HARMFUL because the isolated file loses project context. The immune pipeline consumes these verdicts in Stage 4 and sets `finding.verified = True` for SAFE or NEUTRAL results; that feeds NK bug-closed logic in later rounds, so a falsely-safe isolated eval can prematurely close a bug across the system. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface and directly affects reviewer-facing closure state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the relevant project subtree instead of a single file: copy all `source_paths` into the temp directory preserving relative paths, patch the target file within that copied tree, and run tool/test commands against the copied paths in that temp workspace.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as the summed net delta across tools is non-positive. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues` and returns HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0`. Example from current fields: `+3` new pyright errors, `-3` ruff warnings, `0` bandit gives `total_net == 0`, so with passing/no tests the verdict becomes SAFE/NEUTRAL despite new type errors introduced.
FOLLOW: This is a silent misclassification in the core “fix evaluation” feature. The immune pipeline trusts SAFE/NEUTRAL to mark findings `verified=True`; therefore a fix that regresses correctness or security in one dimension can still be programmatically verified and used to close the bug in NK dedup. Because the PoC goal is reviewer trust in end-to-end signals, cross-tool cancellation is high severity: it can tell the reviewer a fix is safe when the patched file is objectively worse on one checker.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as HARMFUL: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return HARMFUL before considering aggregate reduction.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong source file because it accepts substring matches: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A short mention like `brain.py` or a basename reused in multiple directories will match whichever `source_paths` entry first contains that substring, not the intended file. The regex also scrapes paths from both description and proposed fix text, increasing accidental matches.
FOLLOW: If the wrong file is selected, `evaluate_fix()` reads baseline diagnostics from one file, applies text intended for another, and emits UNEVALUABLE/SAFE/HARMFUL for the wrong target. That poisons fix verification results and can mark an unrelated finding verified in the immune pipeline. Because this function is the only file resolver for sandbox patching, the bug crosses the endocrine→immune boundary and can silently corrupt bug-closure state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve only exact path suffix or exact basename matches, and if multiple matches remain, return UNEVALUABLE instead of choosing the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the “health scan” omits CrossHair entirely even though the module-level contract and tool list explicitly advertise it as part of the endocrine layer (`CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, tool docstring says crosshair exists alongside pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy). There is no `run_crosshair()` implementation and `scan_health()` never invokes it.
FOLLOW: This is not just unused constants; it means one advertised health-scan capability never fires. Reviewers and downstream logic may believe symbolic analysis is part of the inter-round scan when it is absent. The discrepancy also biases fix evaluation and health totals because only syntax/type/lint/security tools contribute. In PoC terms, a claimed feature is dead and reviewer-facing outputs overstate what was checked.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove CrossHair from the endocrine interface and binary declarations for now so the reported capabilities match reality.
VERIFIED: TRUE
